hardware.device: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S Graphics

candidate.description: Keep the production route-parallel selected-down and per-output-tile weighted finalizers, then let the last of 192 tile finalizers execute the exact D9 aggregate/residual/next-RMSNorm tree.
candidate.tail_mapping: two independent production-order logical lanes per physical thread

protocol.timing: 21 counterbalanced HIP-event samples, each the average of 100 launches, after five warmups
protocol.trace_command: rocprofv3 --kernel-trace with one cached control/candidate sample

interpretation.result: The fused finalizer loses both actual-weight family gates despite deleting one launch and preserving every arithmetic bit.
interpretation.mechanism: The local128 finalizer adds a second completion tier and serializes two local256 logical D9 lanes per thread. The candidate keeps VGPR80 and scratch0 but raises LDS from 512 to 1536 bytes; its tail work costs more than the standalone local256 D9 launch.
interpretation.decision: Stop before runtime integration and remove the candidate. Keep the production selected-down kernel plus standalone wave0-tree D9.
interpretation.reopen_only_if: A successor preserves local256-or-wider physical D9 ownership or removes the tail through a different consumer fusion without a last-producer serial section.
